title: Open derived stalk comparison on a literal representative
statement: Let j:Y→Z be an open immersion of schemes, y∈Y, i∈ℤ, and assume derived categories of sheaf modules exist on all schemes. Let N be any sheaf-module cochain complex on Z. Use the constructed comparisons of [def-pc-open-derived-stalk-iso]. The forgotten inverse comparisonStalkHomologyIso on Z, followed by openDerivedStalkIso on Q(N) and additive derived stalk cohomology of openRestrictionRepresentativeIso(j,N).inv, equals the inverse ambient forgetful homology comparison, homology of the inverse additive restrictStalkNatIso evaluated on N.sc i, the restricted forgetful homology comparison, and the forgotten inverse comparisonStalkHomologyIso for the literal restriction of N. This fixes only the value on one representative; no auxiliary complexes, arbitrary chain-square hypothesis or morphism alpha occurs.

proof.text: Expand openDerivedStalkIso and openRestrictionRepresentativeIso. The inverse derived-restriction comparison is followed by its hom through additive derived stalk cohomology, so these two factors cancel.

Move the exact restriction localization factor through additiveStalkCohomologyIso by its inverse naturality. Evaluate restriction.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso on Q(N), using hom_app_Q. The homology image of the inverse localization factor cancels the homology image of its hom.

Evaluate the two exact-stalk comparisons on the complexes. The hom_app_Q formula and comparisonStalkHomologyIso identify each with the short-complex mapHomologyIso followed by the sheaf derived homology factor. Naturality of the inverse restrictStalkNatIso moves that factor across the same-germ map; the two derived homology factors cancel.

Apply ShortComplex.homologyMap_mapNatTrans to the inverse restrictStalkNatIso at N.sc i. For stalk followed by forgetting, compute both homology comparisons with the same mapped left homology data: the kernel object, cokernel object, inclusion and projection are unchanged by whether mapping is done in one or two steps. Thus the composed comparison is the stalk comparison followed by the forgetful one.

Substitute these two composite comparison identities and cancel the invertible stalk comparisons. The surviving factors are the inverse ambient forgetful comparison, homology of the inverse restriction-stalk transformation, the restricted forgetful comparison, and the inverse restricted representative comparison, exactly as stated.

theorem openDerivedStalk_representative_homology
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Y ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j] (y : Y) (i : ℤ)
    (N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace)) ℤ) :
    let F := forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Z.presheaf.stalk (j y))) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
    let F0 := forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
    let S := (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Z.toRingedSpace (j y)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)
    let S0 := (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)
    let R := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let HU := comparisonStalkCohomology Y y i ⋙ F0
    F.map (comparisonStalkHomologyIso Z (j y) N i).inv ≫
        (openDerivedStalkIso j y i).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj N) ≫
        HU.map (openRestrictionRepresentativeIso j N).inv =
      (((S.obj N).sc i).mapHomologyIso F).inv ≫
        ShortComplex.homologyMap
          ((N.sc i).mapNatTrans
            (show (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Z.toRingedSpace (j y) ⋙ F) ⟶
              (openRestrictionFunctor j ⋙
                RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y ⋙ F0) from
              (Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso j y).inv)) ≫
        (((S0.obj (R.obj N)).sc i).mapHomologyIso F0).hom ≫
        F0.map (comparisonStalkHomologyIso Y y (R.obj N) i).inv
